sun.upright:
An Aries Sun wants to go first and be seen going first. The Six of Cups turns that round and points it backwards, at a younger you, an old friend, the street you grew up on. It's a better fit than it looks. This is a Sun card, the Sun sitting in the middle ten degrees of Scorpio, and the Sun is exalted in Aries, which means your sign is where it's most admired and trusted. So the warmth in this card is your own kind of light. It's just been taken somewhere deep and quiet.

Scorpio and Aries sit five signs apart, a quincunx, so they have nothing in common and keep having to adjust to each other. Both have Mars as their ruler, which helps a little, since both want things badly. Aries wants them out loud and straight away, though, and Scorpio wants them in private and for keeps. Fire meeting water doesn't make it easier. You'll probably feel it as a softness that keeps interrupting your drive. You're halfway through planning the next thing and a memory of who you meant to be at fifteen walks in and sits down.

At work this can be an old boss or teacher getting back in touch, or a project you shelved years ago that suddenly looks like the one worth doing. In the family it's often the sibling you used to compete with saying something generous about what you've built. Your body may want the sport you played as a kid. Dig out the ambition you had before anyone told you to be sensible and give it an hour of proper work.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, the Six of Cups can catch an Aries Sun living off an old win. The year you were captain, the business you started at twenty-two, the time you were the youngest person in the room and everyone noticed. The Sun is exalted in Aries, so your sense of yourself as someone who shines runs strong, and when the present isn't giving you that, it's tempting to keep going back to a time when it did.

You'll hear it in yourself telling the same story at every dinner, or measuring a new job against the one where you were a star and finding it flat within a week. Sometimes it goes the other way and you refuse to look back at all, even when an old friend is holding out something good. Ask yourself what you'd start if nobody knew your history, and start a small version of it.

moon.upright:
Aries Moons get over things fast. You feel it, you say it, it's gone, and you're usually a bit baffled by people who are still upset three days later. The Six of Cups brings feelings that don't work that way. They're old and warm and they come up slowly, the smell of a grandparent's kitchen, a song from a school disco, a name you haven't said in years. This card is water and your Moon is fire, and those two elements don't sit easily together.

So there's a bit of a fight going on inside. Part of you wants to feel all of it, and part of you gets impatient and wants to do something instead, text someone, go for a run, clear out a cupboard. The quincunx between Scorpio and Aries makes it harder, because the two signs share no common ground and every feeling has to be translated before you can use it. I've seen Aries Moons treat nostalgia almost like an itch. With this card it helps to let the feeling take longer than you'd normally allow.

In the body it can look like a tiredness that comes from nowhere, or a craving for food you haven't had since you were small. With a parent there may be a softer conversation than usual, and you might be the one to start it. A partner could get a gentler, slower side of you, which they'll probably like. Next time a memory arrives, sit with it for five minutes before you do anything with it.
moon.reversed:
An Aries Moon with this card upside down tends to go one of two ways with the past. Either you slam the door on it, won't talk about childhood, won't go home for the holidays, get irritable when someone gets sentimental. Or you get stuck in an old hurt and keep replaying it with all the heat still in it, years after the other person has forgotten.

Both are fire and water getting tangled. Watch for the moment a sibling or a parent says something that lands like it did when you were twelve, and you react at twelve-year-old speed. It also comes out at night, lying awake running an argument you had a decade ago. Pick the one old grievance that still gets you going and tell a friend the story out loud, all of it, once.

rising.upright:
Aries rising walks into a room like it's already decided something. People read you as quick, direct, maybe a bit much. The Six of Cups softens that front, and others will probably notice before you do. You come across younger and friendlier, easier to approach, the kind of person strangers tell things to in queues. The Sun has a real foothold in your sign, since it's exalted in Aries and also rules the middle decan there, the Three of Wands. So warmth isn't foreign to your manner. It's usually aimed forward.

Here it's aimed back, and that changes how you start things. Scorpio is a quincunx from Aries, five signs away with nothing shared, which is why this can feel a little awkward on you, like wearing someone else's jumper. Instead of charging in you might hesitate, or look for a face you already know in the crowd, or reach for a way of doing things that worked years ago. That's fine. The instinct to go with the familiar is doing you a favour here.

At a job interview or a first meeting, you could find yourself mentioning where you grew up or who you trained under, and it'll warm the room. In dating, you might be drawn to someone who feels oddly familiar, or someone from your past might come back with better timing than last time. Be the one who says hello first to a person you used to know.
rising.reversed:
With this card upside down, Aries rising can end up presenting a younger you than the one who actually exists. You fall back on the jokes, the swagger or the look that worked at twenty-five, and people who've just met you sense something a bit rehearsed. The quick, bold first impression Aries is known for starts to feel like an old habit.

Reunions and new jobs are where it shows most, anywhere you're meeting people and reach for the version of you that used to get the best response. It can also look like refusing help from people who knew you back then, because you'd prefer to arrive looking self-made. Next time you walk into somewhere new, leave the old story at the door and let them meet you as you are this year.

sun.upright:
Taurus sits directly across the wheel from Scorpio, so the Six of Cups comes to a Taurus Sun from the far end of your own axis. Taurus is about what you can hold and keep, Scorpio about what you share and can't let go of, and they're really two views of the same question about attachment. The card's warmth is the Sun in the middle of Scorpio, a warmth for old bonds and long memory. You already know something about that. You're loyal to places, to recipes, to people you've known since primary school.

The Sun has no special standing in Taurus. It's a guest there and takes on the manner of Venus, your ruler, so it shines through comfort and things you can touch. Water and earth get on well, each giving the other shape, and things grow slowly between them. So you'll probably feel a steady pull toward building from what's already yours, the family furniture, the old friend who could become a business partner, the craft you learned from your nan. An opposition always asks for balance, though, and too much of the past can make a Taurus Sun heavy and slow to change.

With money, it can be an inheritance of some kind, even a small or practical one, a set of tools, a recipe book, somebody's good advice. At home it might be restoring something old when you'd normally buy new. In a relationship it's the comfort of a person who knows your history. Choose one thing you own that came from someone you love and use it properly, instead of keeping it in a drawer.
sun.reversed:
The stubborn side of Taurus and the long memory of Scorpio can lock together when this card is reversed. You hold on to the way things were done, the house as it was, the job you had when you felt most yourself, and treat any change as a small betrayal. Because the two signs face each other, it can feel like being pulled two ways, keeping hold and letting go, and Taurus usually picks keeping hold.

Look at your spending first. You might be paying for things that keep an old life going, a car you don't drive, storage for boxes you never open. In friendships it's staying close to someone out of habit long after the warmth has gone. Take one thing you've been keeping for sentimental reasons and ask honestly whether you'd miss it.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon settles down through the senses. You feel safe when the bed's made, the kettle's on and nothing's about to change. The Six of Cups speaks that language well. It's a card of small, kind comforts, a cup of flowers handed from one child to another in the Rider-Waite picture, and it tends to bring back the textures and tastes that made you feel looked after when you were little.

Water and earth are friendly, but Scorpio sits opposite Taurus on the wheel, and that sharpens things. Your Moon wants steady comfort. Scorpio wants depth, and when the card brings the two together the old feelings don't only soothe, they stir. A smell or a song might bring up more than you bargained for, a grandmother's perfume, a certain brand of biscuit. The Sun is only a visitor in Taurus, coloured by Venus, so the warmth comes through pleasure and touch. Let it. A Taurus Moon doesn't have to justify needing a bit of softness.

In the body this is good for sleep and appetite, especially if you go back to the simple food you grew up on. With a parent, there might be an easy afternoon that reminds you why you love them. A partner might please you most by doing something ordinary the way your family used to do it. Cook one meal from your childhood, the whole thing, and eat it slowly with someone.
moon.reversed:
Comfort becomes a hiding place for a Taurus Moon when this card turns over. You go back to the same food, the same shows, the same routine you had years ago, because they're safe, and the safety starts to feel like the only thing you're getting out of your days. With Scorpio opposite your sign, there's often something underneath the comfort that you'd prefer not to feel.

Your body might feel it as sluggishness, eating for memory instead of hunger, sleeping in to avoid the day. At home it can be refusing to change a single room. With family it's letting an old role keep you quiet. Notice which comfort you reach for when you're upset, and once this week try doing something new in its place.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising looks calm from the outside, grounded, unhurried, someone who won't be rushed into a decision. This card makes you come across as more approachable than usual, the friend-of-the-family type people trust within minutes. There's something old-fashioned in how you're presenting yourself too, the kept promise, the handwritten card, the manners somebody taught you.

The card's sign sits opposite your rising, which puts Scorpio on your seventh house, the house of the people you deal with one-to-one. So this card is partly about how others see you and partly about who you're drawn to. Scorpio's intensity comes at you through other people, and the Sun's warmth in that sign turns it into loyalty and history. Earth and water get on, so it's comfortable. You might feel you're being read quite deeply by someone who's only just met you.

It tends to land in partnerships, a business contact who turns out to know your cousin, a date with someone who reminds you of a first love. In your style you might go back to the clothes or the haircut you had when you felt most yourself. Say yes to the person who asks if you remember them, even if it takes you a minute.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Taurus rising can get set in a way of meeting the world that stopped fitting a while ago. You keep the same haircut, the same stories, the same polite reserve, and new people find you pleasant but hard to know. Because Scorpio falls on your seventh, the problem often shows through partners. You may be choosing people who resemble someone from long ago.

Dating and business are where you'll see it. A new contact gets compared to an old one before they've had a chance. A partner is asked, without words, to be the person you lost. Keep your warmth and your manners, which are real, and next time you meet someone, ask them three questions about themselves before you decide who they remind you of.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns tend to live in the present tense, curious about the next thing, the next person, the next idea. The Six of Cups asks you to be curious about the past for once. Scorpio and Gemini are a quincunx apart, five signs with nothing in common, so this doesn't come naturally. Water and air are neutral to each other too, and they need introducing. Once they've met, though, you might find the past is full of stories you haven't told yet.

The Sun is only a guest in Gemini and borrows Mercury's habits, so your light tends to shine through talking, writing, joking, connecting people. Put the Sun in Scorpio's depths next to that and the talking gets slower and more personal. You might want to write something about your family, or call the friend who knew you when you were a completely different person. There's an itch here too, because the card wants you to stay with one feeling and Gemini wants to hop to the next. That's the adjustment the quincunx asks for.

At work it can be a return to an old skill, a language you studied at school, a kind of writing you used to be good at. With siblings, and Gemini's often close to them, there's a chance for a better conversation than you've had in years. In friendship it's the group chat from school suddenly waking up. Write down one story from your childhood exactly as it happened and show it to someone who was there.
sun.reversed:
The card reversed can make a Gemini Sun charming about the past without ever being honest about it. You have a funny story for everything that happened back then, and the jokes keep anyone from getting close to what actually hurt. The Sun rules the last decan of Gemini, the Ten of Swords, which knows a lot about endings. This card upside down tends to dodge them.

At family gatherings you're the entertaining one and nobody asks how you are. At work you might be recycling an old idea because it went down well once. With friends, you might keep people from different parts of your past well apart, so no one sees all of you. Tell one person the part of an old story you usually leave out.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon calms down by talking it through. You need to name a feeling before you can feel it, and you get restless if there's no one to tell. The Six of Cups brings the kind of feeling that's hard to put into words, homesickness for a place that doesn't exist any more, sudden fondness for someone you've lost touch with. It's Scorpio water with the Sun lit inside it, and it goes deeper than your Moon usually goes.

Air and water have no natural ease with each other, and the quincunx between the two signs means your usual tools don't quite fit. So you might find yourself chattering about something small while a much bigger feeling sits underneath. The Sun is a visitor in Gemini, coloured by Mercury, and it keeps wanting to explain. Let the explanation come later. Old letters, old photos, old voicemails can do some of the work for you, because they let the feeling arrive through something you can read.

At night you might dream about school, or a house you lived in as a kid. A sibling or cousin is a likely person to share it with, since they remember the same things and won't need it explained. In the body it can come up as restlessness, a need to walk while you think. Find an old photo, send it to someone who's in it, and don't add a caption.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, this card can leave a Gemini Moon talking about feelings instead of having them. You can describe your childhood beautifully, analyse your family with real skill, and still feel strangely blank when you do. Scorpio's depth and Gemini's quickness are a quincunx apart, and here they've stopped trying to meet.

Sometimes it goes the other way, and you get lost scrolling old photos and old messages at two in the morning, reading back conversations with someone who's gone. That's a Gemini Moon trying to feel through information. You'll notice it in poor sleep, in a phone you can't put down, in a sibling you only ever talk to about practical things. Put the phone in another room one night and let yourself miss what you miss without looking at it.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising meets people quickly and lightly, with a question, a joke, a bit of useful information. The Six of Cups on that doorway makes you seem younger and easier to talk to. There's a playfulness in how you come across, the kid who'd share their lunch with a stranger, and people tend to relax around it. It's an unusual look on you, since Gemini's first move is normally to be clever.

Scorpio is a quincunx from Gemini, five signs apart, so the card's depth and your quick surface don't share much. Air and water meet as strangers and have to be introduced. You might notice that conversations you'd normally keep breezy slip into something more personal than you intended, where you grew up, what your dad was like, the friend you lost touch with. The Sun is a guest in your rising sign and works through Mercury, so the warmth comes out in words. It's a nice change, and a little exposing.

In a new job, you may bond with someone over a shared hometown or school. With neighbours, and Gemini rising often knows all of them, small kindnesses might go back and forth. Online you could be finding old contacts or being found. Next time someone asks where you're from, give them the long answer.
rising.reversed:
With this card reversed, Gemini rising can come across as someone performing an earlier version of themselves. The quick wit that worked at uni gets rolled out at a work dinner and falls a bit flat, or you keep bringing up the old days with people who weren't there. It's air and water failing to meet, the chatter staying light while something heavier goes unsaid.

First meetings and social media are the usual places, the way you present yourself online stuck a few years back. There can also be a habit of reaching for old friends when new ones are right there asking to be let in. Update one small thing about how you introduce yourself, even just the job title or the town, so it matches the life you're living.

sun.upright:
Cancer and Scorpio are both water signs, four apart, a trine, and the Six of Cups comes to a Cancer Sun speaking your own language. This is the sign that keeps the photo albums and remembers everyone's birthday. Your sense of who you are is tied up with where you came from and who looked after you, and this card lights all of that up.

The Sun is a visitor in Cancer, coloured by the Moon, your ruler, so your light has always been a bit reflected, shining most when it's looking after someone. The same element on both sides amplifies everything, for better and for too much. You'll feel proud of your family, your history, the care you've given. You might also feel the old ache for a time that seemed safer, and if you're a Cancer Sun who's been working hard to build something new, the pull back toward home can feel like a test of whether you've really left.

In the family it's often a gathering that goes well, or a reunion that reminds you what kind of person you are when you're with your own. At work the card favours anything that looks after people, especially children. It could be a good time to take a younger colleague under your wing and show them how things are done. With money, you may feel like spending on the house or on something that belonged to a parent. Invite someone from your childhood over and cook for them.
sun.reversed:
A Cancer Sun is always at some risk of making the past its whole identity, and this card reversed turns that up. You might be defining yourself entirely as someone's child, parent or carer, or holding a family story so tightly that it can't change even when you do. With both signs in water, the feeling comes in like a flood and doesn't drain away.

It can look like homesickness that won't pass, or like holding family traditions too rigidly, insisting Christmas be exactly as it was when you were eight. At work it can be mothering people who didn't ask for it. With a partner, it might be expecting them to fit into your family the way it's always been. Ask yourself what you'd want to be known for if nobody knew your family, and write down the first answer.

moon.upright:
Your Moon is in the sign the Moon rules, which makes you feel everything fully and remember all of it. The Six of Cups on a Cancer Moon is almost too much of a good thing. Scorpio and Cancer are trine, both water, and the Sun inside this card warms that water until old feelings rise easily and gently. You're likely to feel very tender, and very aware of how much you love the people who shaped you.

The trouble with water on water is that nothing gives it edges. The Sun has no dignity of its own in Cancer and takes on the Moon's colouring, so even the card's warmth arrives as mood and memory. A song in a shop can put you back in your mum's car at eight years old, and you'll be a bit teary the rest of the afternoon. That's fine. It's a Cancer Moon doing what it does best, keeping hold of love. The only thing to watch is whether you're still in the room with the people who are here.

Sleep may be full of dreams about old houses. Your appetite might pull toward comfort food, which is alright in moderation. With a parent or grandparent there could be a conversation you'll keep for years. In a relationship you'll want to be babied a little, and it's worth asking for that plainly. Ring the oldest person in your family and ask them what you were like as a baby.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the Six of Cups can flood a Cancer Moon with a longing it can't do much with. You miss people who are still alive but have changed, places that are still there but aren't yours, a family that used to be whole. Water on water, with no fire or earth to give it shape, means the feeling can go round and round without ever landing.

Late nights and family occasions are the worst of it, and often the body carries it as a heavy, low tiredness. It can also look like guarding your mother's version of events, or your own old hurt, so fiercely that nobody gets to talk about it differently. Do something with your hands when it comes up, bake, garden, fix something, so the feeling has somewhere to go.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising is guarded at the door and soft once you're let in. People often read you as shy, or careful, or quietly kind. This card lets the soft part show sooner. You come across like someone's favourite aunt or the friend who always has a spare jumper, and strangers are likely to tell you things they don't tell most people.

The card and your rising share water and sit a trine apart, which is about as easy as astrology gets. With Cancer rising the Moon is your chart ruler, and the Sun passing through your sign takes on its moods, so the warmth you give off depends a lot on how you're feeling. Because it's the same element twice over, it's amplified. You'll be very good at making people feel at home. You might also be quick to feel rejected if they don't return it.

At work you're the one who remembers the tea orders and the kids' names. With new people you might be looking for a family feeling, a group to belong to. With a neighbour, a plate of something home-made could start a real friendship. In your style there may be something with a history, a family ring, an old coat. When someone new is clearly nervous, be the person who shows them where everything is.
rising.reversed:
The protective shell Cancer rising is known for can get thicker with this card reversed. Having been soft with people before and hurt for it, you might meet new people as if they're about to do the same thing, polite and pleasant and completely closed. Or, and this happens too, you latch onto someone new too quickly because they remind you of a person who used to feel like home.

First meetings, new jobs and new neighbourhoods are where it shows. You might keep the same small circle you had at school and never really let anyone else join. With the card and your rising both in water, the feeling behind it is strong and worth taking seriously. Pick one new person and let them in a little further than you normally would, a proper coffee, a real answer to how you are.

sun.upright:
This is a Sun card, and the Sun is your ruler, so when the Six of Cups turns up for a Leo Sun it comes with the landlord's authority. It's the only sign where the card's planet is fully at home. What's odd is where that Sun is standing in the card, in the middle of Scorpio, a fixed water sign square to yours. Your light, which normally wants a stage, has been sent somewhere private and old.

Leo and Scorpio are both fixed and three signs apart, and squares like that make friction that forces something to move. Fire and water don't help. You'll feel it as a pull between wanting to be admired for who you are and wanting to be loved for who you were, by the people who knew you before you were anyone. Leo Suns are generous with warmth, sometimes a bit showily. This card asks for the quieter kind, the gift given without an audience, and I've seen Leos find that surprisingly moving once they let it happen.

Creatively it can mean going back to what you loved making as a child, the drawing, the drama club, the terrible band. With children, your own or someone else's, it's a lovely time to teach them something you were taught. A parent might need you to shine for them in a small way, turning up, telling them what you've done. Give someone a present this week and don't tell anyone else about it.
sun.reversed:
Pride and nostalgia make a strong mix, and with the card reversed a Leo Sun can start living off its own legend. The school captaincy, the year the band nearly made it, the time the whole family said you'd be famous. The Sun rules Leo, so your need to shine is strong and real, and when the present isn't feeding it, the past gets polished until it glows.

At reunions you need to have done best. With your own kids it can be pushing them toward the childhood you had, or the one you wish you'd had. In creative work it's remaking the thing that worked instead of risking something new. The square from Scorpio means the hurt of not being noticed any more goes deep, even if you'd never admit it. Make one thing this month that nobody from your past would expect from you.

moon.upright:
Being adored is what settles a Leo Moon, openly, warmly, and preferably by someone who's known you a long time. The Six of Cups has a lot of that kind of love in it. Old friends remembering what you were like at twelve, a parent proud of you out loud, a kid who's decided you're the best person in the world. The Sun is in its own sign in Leo, and it's this card's planet too, which is why the feeling runs so warm.

The square from Scorpio complicates it. Your Moon's feelings are fire, big and immediate and out in the open, and this card's are water, slow and deep and kept. So you might feel something about the past that you can't turn into a performance or even a good story, and that's unsettling for a Leo Moon. The tension is useful. It lets you feel something privately, without needing anyone to watch, and Leo Moons don't often get to do that.

With family it comes through in the old jokes and the story everyone tells about you at every gathering. In romance, you might want to go back to places you've been happy with your partner. Your body wants play, singing in the car, a game in the park, and it's worth giving in to. Tell someone who loves you the one childhood memory you've never mentioned.
moon.reversed:
When the card is upside down, a Leo Moon can sulk about the past. Nobody makes a fuss of you the way your family used to, your partner doesn't look at you the way they did at the start, and friends seem to have forgotten how much fun you were. Scorpio's square to Leo means the hurt gets held onto, and the Sun's warmth turns into a slow burn.

Birthdays disappoint. You fish for compliments by bringing up old glories, and feel sidelined when a sibling gets the attention. At work it can be missing the boss who thought you were brilliant. The body can feel it as a drop in energy, a kind of flatness. Instead of waiting to be celebrated, plan a celebration yourself, for somebody else, and enjoy their face when it works.

rising.upright:
Picture the older child in the card, leaning down to hand over a cup full of white flowers. That's roughly how you're meeting people with this card on Leo rising, generous, a little protective, making a small gesture feel like an occasion. The Sun rules Leo, so with Leo rising it's also your chart ruler, and a Sun card here goes straight to the front of how you present.

The friction comes from Scorpio, square to Leo and fixed like you, which means neither sign moves easily. Leo rising likes to be seen, and Scorpio would prefer not to be seen at all. Put water under fire and your usual confident entrance gets a softer, more personal edge. You might care much less about impressing strangers and find yourself noticing who's kind to the waiter. That can feel like losing your touch. It usually isn't. People trust you faster when you come across like this.

At work you could be the one who welcomes a new starter and remembers the details of their first week. In your style there may be a throwback, a colour you wore at school, your dad's watch. Old friends will probably find you easy to reconnect with. Next time you walk into a room, look for the person standing on their own and go and talk to them first.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising can end up playing the part it was cast in years ago when this card turns over. The class clown, the golden child, the one with the best stories. You arrive with the old routine polished and ready, and new people feel entertained without feeling met. The square from Scorpio means something private is going on behind the show, and it's getting harder to keep out of view.

At work this might be leaning on charm when the job needs something new from you. In dating it's the same opening lines and the same stories, getting the same results. Friends from way back may be the only ones who see past it. Go somewhere you're not known and let yourself be quieter than usual, just to see who talks to you.

sun.upright:
There's usually a Virgo Sun in any family who knows where the old photos are, who kept the school reports and can tell you exactly which year Nan's recipe changed. The Six of Cups warms that part of you. Scorpio and Virgo are two signs apart, a sextile, which is a friendly, cooperative angle, and water and earth feed each other. So the card sits well with you, as long as you actually do something with it.

The Sun has a real foothold in your sign. It's only a visitor in Virgo, coloured by Mercury, but it also rules the first ten degrees, the decan of the Eight of Pentacles, the card of careful work and practice. So your light tends to come through craft, through getting things right. What this card adds is feeling. You might find yourself caring about the past in a way that can't be sorted or filed, missing someone's handwriting, wanting to fix a thing because your grandad would have. That can unsettle a sign that likes to be useful.

At work it could be going back to a skill you learnt young and were good at, sewing, woodwork, maths. With money, it's a good time to sort out old accounts or something a relative left in a mess. In the body, the routines you had as a kid, early nights, a walk after dinner, would do you good. Choose one thing from your family's past and restore it properly, even if it takes weeks.
sun.reversed:
Virgo Suns can turn the past into a list of mistakes. With this card reversed you might be going back over old decisions, auditing your childhood, correcting other people's memories of events, all with an anxious precision that never quite lets anything be sweet. The sextile between the signs is an opening, and here it's being used to pick at things.

Family gatherings are where it's loudest, when you're the one who says that's not how it happened. At work it's redoing old projects instead of letting them stand, or holding yourself to standards set by a teacher you haven't seen in twenty years. Physically it can look like a knot in the stomach whenever home comes up. Find one memory you've been correcting for years and let someone else's version stand without comment.

moon.upright:
The Six of Cups is a card about small things done kindly, and a Virgo Moon knows that better than most. You feel safe when things are in order, when someone's thought of the details, when a cup of tea arrives made the right way without you asking. Water and earth get along, and Scorpio sits a sextile from Virgo, so the card lands gently and gives your feelings a bit more depth than usual.

Virgo Moons often look after everyone else before they notice what they need. The Sun is only passing through Virgo, taking on Mercury's colour, which is why the warmth here tends to come out as helpfulness. The card might bring back a memory of being looked after properly, a nurse, a teacher, an aunt who noticed you were quiet, and you might feel a bit teary about it without knowing why. You're allowed to be the one who's cared for. The sextile makes that easy, though you still have to say yes when someone offers.

In the body this is a good time for gentle routines, a proper breakfast, an early night, the walk you used to do. With a friend it's a chance to let them help. At work, someone older may show you a way of doing something that makes your life easier. When someone offers to do something for you, say yes and don't fix it afterwards.
moon.reversed:
Worry is the usual shape this card takes for a Virgo Moon when it turns over. The past becomes a place to check for faults, the thing you said at a dinner five years ago, the way you handled a parent's illness, the friend you think you let down. Water and earth usually help each other, and here the feeling gets stuck in the ground and turns to fretting.

You'll feel it in your sleep first, lying awake running old conversations. You'll see it in over-cleaning, over-planning, keeping busy so the sadness can't catch up. With family, it can look like being the helper so you never have to be helped. Write down the memory you keep checking, and next to it, the kindest true thing someone would say about it.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising comes across as capable, neat and a little reserved, the person who's already read the instructions. This card warms the whole look. The Six of Cups on your rising makes you seem helpful in a gentler way, and people will want to ask you for small favours because you look glad to do them. Strangers who'd normally find you a bit exacting will pick up on the kindness underneath first.

The Sun rules the first decan of Virgo, the Eight of Pentacles, so it's no stranger to your sign even though it's only a guest there, taking on Mercury's habits. Scorpio is sextile Virgo and water feeds earth, which means the card's warmth sits easily on your surface. Your instinct is to start things carefully. This card might have you starting them the way you were taught, by a parent, a first boss, someone who showed you how to hold a pen properly. Going with that borrowed method usually works well for you.

In a new workplace, you could be the one who shows others the ropes, and they'll remember you kindly for it. In your style, something handmade or inherited might become part of how you present. With neighbours or acquaintances, small exchanges of help can build into real friendships. Offer to teach someone new a thing you know well, without being asked.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising gets a bit fussy about the old way of doing things when this card is upside down. You arrive with the method you learnt years ago and a slight air of disapproval when others do it differently. The sextile between the signs is meant to help, and here it's closed off. People might find you helpful and hard to warm to.

A new job is where it tends to surface, with you saying how they did it at your last place. In friendships you might be the one who organises the reunion and then criticises the venue. It can also be a kind of shyness, where helping is the only way you know to be with people you've just met, and you hide behind it. Let one thing be done badly and stay warm about it.

sun.upright:
Libra is the sign where the Sun is in fall, which means it struggles to be heard and has to find a roundabout way to do its job. A lot of Libra Suns know that feeling. You make everyone else comfortable and forget to take up room yourself. The Six of Cups is a Sun card, so this matters here, and it asks where your sense of who you are went while you were busy being fair to everyone.

Scorpio is Libra's next-door neighbour, the sign that follows yours on the wheel, and neighbours like that have little in common and each has what the other lacks. You have the grace. Scorpio has the depth. Water and air need to be introduced. What you might feel is a longing for a time before you learnt to smooth everything over, when you just liked what you liked. There's a gentleness in this card that suits you, the gift offered for the pleasure of it, and it can make you oddly homesick for your own younger opinions.

In love, it can be an old flame reappearing, and you'll need to ask yourself honestly whether it's them you miss or who you were with them. With friends, it's the ones from school who remember you as bossier than you are now. At work, an old idea of yours might be worth bringing back with your name on it. Say out loud one thing you liked as a child that you've since pretended not to.
sun.reversed:
The card reversed can have a Libra Sun keeping the peace with the past at its own expense. You go along with the family story, the way your parents' divorce is told, the idea that you were the easy child, because disagreeing would upset things. With the Sun in fall in Libra, your own view of what happened can get very quiet.

Relationships are the first place to look. Going back to an ex because it's familiar and the breakup felt unfair is typical. So is staying friends with someone you've outgrown because ending it would feel unkind. At work, you might agree to an old way of doing things you never liked. Pick one old family story where your memory differs and, gently, tell someone your version.

moon.upright:
Libra Moons feel safe when things are pleasant between people. An argument in the house can put you off your food. This card brings the sort of feeling that comes easily to you, gentle, affectionate, a warm exchange where nobody's keeping score. That's the card's meaning in a sentence, and it's close to what your Moon wants most.

It isn't completely easy, though. The card's Sun is in fall in your sign, uncomfortable and often unheard, and the depth Scorpio brings sits next door to Libra, a neighbour with a different temperament. So underneath the nice feelings there can be older ones, the times as a child you kept quiet to keep the peace, the fights you listened to through a wall. The card warms that up. It may bring back memories you didn't expect to be moved by, and a Libra Moon might try to tidy them into something nice before they've been properly felt.

With a partner, this favours tenderness, small gifts, flowers, a note left on the bench. With a parent there might be a softer moment than you've had in a while. In the body it's rest and beauty, a bath, music you loved at sixteen. Let yourself feel one sad memory all the way through without making it pretty.
moon.reversed:
People-pleasing is the trap for a Libra Moon with this card reversed. You might be comforting yourself with how nice things used to be with someone, and making excuses for how they are with you now. Or you're holding onto a friendship because the history is lovely even though the present is thin. The Sun in fall in Libra finds it hard to say what it needs.

This lands mainly in relationships. It might be a partner you're still with because of how it was in the first year, or a parent whose moods you still manage as if you were ten. The body can carry it as tension in the neck and shoulders. Say one small true thing you need to someone who's used to hearing that you're fine.

rising.upright:
The first thing people notice about Libra rising is usually the charm. You're easy to talk to, well put together, good at making strangers feel welcome. The Six of Cups adds something sweet and a bit old-fashioned. You might come across like someone who writes thank-you cards and still sees their school friends, which you may well be.

The Sun is in fall in Libra, so its warmth doesn't come through directly for you. It finds an indirect route, through courtesy, through little kindnesses, through making sure everyone's had a turn. Scorpio sits next to Libra on the wheel, and neighbouring signs like these have little in common. The card's depth might make your usual lightness feel a bit thin to you. You could find yourself wanting a real conversation with people you'd normally keep things polite with, and noticing that they want it too.

At a work do, it might be you who reconnects two old colleagues. In dating, someone could remind you of a first love, and there's a sweetness in that worth enjoying for what it is. With your style, it can be something borrowed from a parent or an older sibling. Send a note to someone who was kind to you years ago and tell them what it meant.
rising.reversed:
This card upside down can make Libra rising seem charming in a slightly dated way, polite, pleasant and hard to reach. You're relying on manners you learnt as a kid to keep everyone happy, and the Sun in fall in Libra means that what you really think stays out of sight. Air and water haven't been introduced here, so the feeling and the manners stay in separate rooms.

New relationships are where it costs you, since you're so busy being agreeable that the other person doesn't get to meet you. Going along with a friend's plan because it's what you always did together is part of it. With colleagues, it can mean smiling through something that bothers you. Give your opinion first sometimes, before you've checked what the other person thinks.

sun.upright:
The Six of Cups belongs to your sign. It's the card of the middle ten degrees of Scorpio, the decan the Sun rules, so drawing it for a Scorpio Sun is a bit like being handed something from your own house. If your birthday falls in that middle stretch, it's closer still. The Sun has no special dignity in Scorpio and takes on the colour of Mars, your traditional ruler, or Pluto if you use the modern one, which gives even its warmth some intensity.

Scorpio Suns remember everything, and that's usually talked about as a warning, the grudges, the long silences. This card shows the other side of that memory. You also remember every kindness, the teacher who stood up for you, the friend who turned up in the worst week, and you're loyal to those people for life. Water on water amplifies, for better and for too much, so the tenderness might be almost overwhelming, and you may want to hide it. Try not to hide it from the people concerned.

At work, loyalty is the theme, someone from years back vouching for you or you vouching for them. With money, it can be sorting out something shared with family, a house, an inheritance, and doing it generously. In love it's a deepening, the sense of being known over time. Go back to someone who was good to you when you were young and thank them in detail.
sun.reversed:
The long memory of a Scorpio Sun can turn on itself with this card reversed. Old hurts get kept as carefully as old kindnesses, maybe more carefully, and the past becomes a place you guard. It's your own decan card, so this is Scorpio's shadow at close range, the loyalty that won't let go even when letting go would help.

Family is the likeliest place, a falling-out that's gone on for years because nobody wants to be the first to call. In love, it might be keeping an ex's letters or comparing a partner to someone who hurt you. At work, you might refuse to trust anyone new because of what happened last time. Choose one old grudge and put it down for a week, just to feel what that's like.

moon.upright:
Someone with a Scorpio Moon feels things deeply and privately, and doesn't hand out trust to many people. This card, native to your own sign, brings the sort of feeling you know well, only warmed. It's the Sun sitting in Scorpio's middle decan, taking on Mars's colouring (or Pluto's), and it lets old feelings rise slowly and softly for once, without the usual edge.

Being water on water, it amplifies, and that cuts both ways. You might feel more tender toward people from your past than you've let yourself feel in years, someone you fell out with, a grandparent, a first love. The softness can be a relief. It can also feel risky for a Scorpio Moon, because you know how much you feel, and letting it show means being seen. I see this a lot with Scorpio Moons. The feeling is there, it's lovely, and they spend half their energy keeping it private.

In the body, it can show up as needing more sleep, and deeper sleep, with dreams of old places. With a partner there might be a moment of real closeness when you tell them something from childhood you've never told anyone. With a parent there may be a thaw. Let one person see you moved by something from the past, and don't explain it away afterwards.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed on a Scorpio Moon can pull you down into the past and keep you there. You go over an old betrayal, or grieve someone in private and tell no one, or keep checking on an ex's life from a distance. With the same element on both sides, the feeling has nothing to stop it and nowhere to drain off.

It's often worst at night and in quiet stretches, the weekend with nothing planned, the drive home. With family it can come out as a coldness nobody understands the reason for. Physically there can be a heaviness, a kind of exhaustion. Tell one person you trust what you've been going over, even just the outline of it, so it isn't only yours to carry.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising usually gives off something watchful. People can find you hard to read at first, even a bit intimidating, and you like it that way. The Six of Cups, your rising sign's own card for its middle decan, softens that without taking it away. You might come across as quiet but kind, the person who notices who's been left out and gets them a drink.

The Sun's a guest in Scorpio, shaped by Mars (or Pluto), so its warmth comes through intensity, focus, full attention. With the same element on both sides, it's strong. What you might notice is that you're letting people in faster than usual, and it feels safer than you expected. Old instincts are guiding you too. You may trust someone on sight because they remind you of someone you trusted as a child, and with this card that tends to be a good instinct. Strangers will notice the difference quickly.

In your working life, a new client or colleague may turn out to have a connection to your past. In friendships, someone you haven't seen in years might get back in touch. In your style, you might choose something softer or more nostalgic than your usual black. Next time you meet someone new, tell them one small true thing about where you come from.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising already keeps its guard up, and with this card reversed the guard can be an old one, put up years ago for reasons that no longer apply. You meet new people as if they're the people who hurt you, and they feel the chill without knowing why. Being your sign's own decan card, it shows your sign's old habit very plainly.

New jobs and first dates bring it out, and any room where you're sizing people up. It can also be the opposite, trusting someone too fast because they feel familiar, and missing the signs. It helps to assume, when you walk in somewhere new, that the people there are strangers with no connection to your past, and see what changes.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns are usually looking at the horizon, the next trip, the next big idea, the place they haven't been yet. So the Six of Cups can feel like being asked to turn round in the car. Scorpio is the sign just before yours on the wheel, a neighbour with a very different temperament, and each of you has what the other lacks. You have range. Scorpio has roots and memory, and this card brings you some of those.

Water and fire are opposed elements, which is where the friction sits. Your fire wants to move, and this card's water wants to stay and feel. The Sun is only a visitor in Sagittarius and takes on Jupiter's manner, generous, big-hearted, optimistic, so it's easy for you to be warm about the past. It's harder to stay in it long enough to learn something. You might notice you've started telling stories about where you grew up, or wanting to go back to somewhere you went as a kid, and that's worth following.

Travel is the obvious place this lands, a return visit to a town you left, a holiday with family that feels like the old ones. In study, you might return to a subject you dropped. With friends, the one who knew you before you left home may have something to teach you now. Book the trip back to one place that shaped you, even if it's only an hour's drive.
sun.reversed:
Sagittarius can be very good at leaving, and with this card reversed the leaving might be how you deal with the past. You moved away, you changed jobs, you started over, and each time you told yourself the old stuff didn't matter. Fire and water are opposed, so the feeling gets boiled off before it can land. Jupiter, colouring the Sun in your sign, makes everything bigger, including the story you tell about why you had to go.

You'll spot it when family asks when you're coming home, or when an old friend gets in touch and you're vague about meeting. At the other extreme, it can be romanticising a gap year or a time abroad until nothing since measures up. Ring someone from the place you left and ask how things really are there.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon feels best with room to move. Freedom, a bit of adventure, a joke to break the tension. The Six of Cups brings the opposite sort of comfort, the kind you get from staying still somewhere familiar with people who've known you forever. It's the fire of your Moon meeting the water of this card, and those two elements usually fight.

What you'll probably feel is a surprising homesickness. You, the one who's always keen to go, might want your mum's cooking or the town you couldn't wait to leave. Scorpio sits beside Sagittarius on the wheel, and neighbours like that each carry what the other misses. The Sun is a guest in your sign and borrows Jupiter's generosity, so the warmth here tends to feel expansive and a bit sentimental. It's alright to be sentimental. A Sagittarius Moon often laughs it off, which is a shame.

Your body may want to sleep in a familiar bed, or walk somewhere you used to walk. With friends it might be an old one visiting and staying up talking far too late. At work, you might find yourself missing an old team more than you expected. With family, your stories from abroad may land better than usual. When you're homesick, phone home before you talk yourself out of it.
moon.reversed:
Restlessness is the usual cover for this card reversed on a Sagittarius Moon. You feel a pang for somewhere or someone, and instead of feeling it you book something, plan something, go somewhere. The water keeps putting out your fire, and you keep lighting new ones so you don't have to stop. The Sun takes Jupiter's colouring in your sign, and Jupiter overdoes things, so the escape plans tend to get bigger each time.

It also comes out as being breezy with family, jokey about the past when someone's trying to talk seriously, or romanticising a time you were free. With friends, you might be the one who's always away when something important happens. At night you might feel oddly low with no idea why. Sit with an old photo for ten minutes before you make any new plans, and notice what you feel.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks into a room like it's already having a good time. Open, funny, a bit loud, ready to talk to anyone. The Six of Cups softens the edges. People might find you gentler than they expected, and curious about them, and the humour turns affectionate, the kind that reminds everyone of a shared joke from years back. Sagittarius rising is usually the one telling the story. Here you're just as likely to be asking for one.

Scorpio is your neighbour on the wheel, the sign just behind yours, and the card's depth sits at your back like something you walked away from. Fire and water are at odds. So there's an odd tension in how you're meeting people, where you're still enthusiastic and outgoing but something older is showing through. The Sun visiting your sign works through Jupiter, which means the warmth is generous. Someone might meet you and feel they've known you for years.

At work, this is good for any role where you're welcoming people, teaching, guiding, showing someone around. In your personal life, an old travel companion may turn up. In how you present yourself, you might go back to something from an earlier chapter, a hat, a way of dressing from when you were first on your own. Say yes to a reunion you'd normally skip.
rising.reversed:
This card turned over can have Sagittarius rising acting like the life of the party it used to be. The same anecdotes, the same big entrance, the same tales from a trip ten years ago. New people are entertained for a bit and then feel they've heard it all. The fire of your rising and the water of this card aren't working together, and the Sun, taking on Jupiter's colouring here, makes the stories bigger with each telling.

Dinner parties and new jobs are where it happens, the old routine filling the space before anyone can get to know you. Always being on the move keeps people at arm's length too. Let someone new ask you a question and answer it with something that happened this year.

sun.upright:
The children in the Six of Cups aren't doing anything useful. One is giving the other some flowers in a cup, and that's the whole picture. For a Capricorn Sun, whose sense of self tends to be built on what you've achieved and what you're responsible for, that's worth thinking about. Scorpio and Capricorn are a sextile apart, a friendly angle, and water and earth feed each other. The card will fit you well if you let it.

The Sun is only passing through Capricorn and takes on Saturn's colouring, which makes your light slow, serious and earned. It also rules the last decan of your sign, the Four of Pentacles, the card of holding tight to what you have. So you know how to keep things. What this card asks is whether you can give something away for the pleasure of it. I've seen this with Capricorn Suns often. There's a softer person in there who got sensible very young, maybe too young, and this card goes looking for them.

At work, a mentor or an old colleague might open a door, and it's worth letting them. With money, you might want to spend on something that's pure pleasure for once, or on a family member without it being a loan. With a parent, especially one who held a lot of authority in your childhood, a warmer conversation is possible. Do one thing for a whole afternoon purely because you enjoyed it when you were ten.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with this card reversed might be looking back at the past as a list of lessons, or as a time you had to grow up too fast, and holding it against yourself or someone else. The Sun rules your sign's Four of Pentacles decan, and here that clenched quality comes through. You keep things, including old resentments about who didn't help.

With money it can mean being tight with family because of something that happened years ago. At work it can look like doing everything the way your first boss did, because that's how it's done. With your own children, if you have them, it might be expecting them to be as responsible as you had to be. Let someone help you with something you'd normally do alone, and let it be done their way.

moon.upright:
Capricorn Moons tend to feel safe when they're in control, when the bills are paid and the plan is working. Feelings are often kept for later, or for never. The Six of Cups gets past that more easily than most cards, because water and earth work well together and the sextile from Scorpio is a friendly one. The feeling it brings is steady and warm, and it asks for nothing back.

What surprises Capricorn Moons with this card is how young the feeling is. You might remember being small and looked after, before you started looking after yourself, and it can bring a lump to the throat. The Sun is a guest in your Moon's sign, taking Saturn's colour, so even the warmth feels solid and a little serious. That makes it easier to trust. You're allowed to rest in it. The sextile is an opening, though, and you do have to take it.

In the body this is a good time for rest you don't have to earn, a nap, a lie-in, a long bath. With parents, an old photo or a family story might bring you closer. At home, you may want to bring out something old and treasured and put it where you can see it. When you notice you're tired, stop, even if the list isn't finished.
moon.reversed:
Holding the past at arm's length is how a Capricorn Moon tends to handle this card reversed, because it's easier than feeling it. You were the responsible one, you coped, and going back over any of that feels pointless and a bit indulgent. Saturn's colouring on the Sun in your sign dries the warmth up into duty. Water and earth normally help each other, and here the ground is too hard for the water to get in.

You'll often see it with parents, where you do everything that's needed and never actually talk. It might show in the body as tightness, a tired back, a jaw you clench at night. With a partner, it can look like being useful instead of close. Ask one person who knew you as a child what you were like before you got so serious.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising usually comes across as older than its years. Serious, reliable, someone who'll turn up on time and do what they said. The Six of Cups tends to take a few years off that impression. You might seem more playful, or kinder in a way that's easier to see, and people who'd normally find you a bit formidable will warm to you quickly.

With Capricorn rising, Saturn rules your chart, and the Sun passing through your sign takes on its colouring, so the warmth here is steady and understated. Scorpio sits sextile to Capricorn, and the card's water softens your earth without washing anything away. It's an easy opening. What you'll notice is that your instinct is to reach back for something that worked, an old contact, a method you learnt early, a way of dressing that feels like you. It serves you well here, and it's usually quicker than starting from nothing.

At work, it's a good time to get back in touch with someone you trained with or who gave you your first break. In friendships, you might be more relaxed with people who knew you before you got so busy. On a first date, talk about where you grew up. Wear or carry one thing that belonged to someone older in your family.
rising.reversed:
Reversed, the card can make Capricorn rising look like it's still following rules set by someone long gone. You arrive composed and correct and slightly stiff, doing things the way you were taught, and new people see competence without much warmth. The sextile is there as an opening and it isn't being used. It's the Saturn side of you stuck in an old role.

It can show up in a new job, where you're the one pointing out how things should be done. At social events, you might hang back and do the dishes rather than join in. With people from your past, you could be distant because you don't want to seem soft. Say something warm to a colleague you respect, plainly and without making a joke of it.

sun.upright:
The Sun is in detriment in Aquarius, sitting in the sign opposite its home, so it works against the grain and the effort shows. Plenty of Aquarius Suns will know what that feels like. You shine by being different, by stepping back, by being fair to everyone at once, and being personally warm can be harder than it looks. The Six of Cups is a Sun card, and it brings all of that up.

Scorpio and Aquarius are both fixed and three signs apart, a square, which means friction that forces something to shift. Scorpio holds on to people and the past. Aquarius prefers the future and the group. Water and air are neutral and have to be introduced. What you might feel is a pull to be sentimental about one specific person or place, and it can make you uneasy because it's so personal. You don't have to explain it. A lot of Aquarius Suns find, with this card, that they miss someone more than they'd admitted.

With friends, it can be an old group from school or uni coming back together, and you being more moved by it than you'd planned. At work, something you cared about years ago, a cause, an invention, might be worth picking back up. With family, it's a chance to be warm without being ironic about it. Keep one sentimental thing on your desk and don't explain it to anyone who asks.
sun.reversed:
With the Sun in detriment in Aquarius, the warmth of this card can get stuck behind your detachment when it's reversed. You look at your own past like a case study, interesting, a bit odd, not really about you. Friends from long ago feel like people from another life, and you're quietly relieved not to see them.

Or you swing the opposite way and get very attached to one version of the future you imagined at twenty, the life you were going to have, and keep measuring against it. Old friends and family reunions are where this surfaces, and at work it's the idea you won't drop. Get in touch with one person you drifted from and see who they've become.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon often feels safest with a bit of distance. You care a lot, but you like to care from a step away, where you can think clearly. The Six of Cups closes that gap. It brings the sort of feeling that's close up and personal, the smell of a grandparent's house, an old friend's laugh, and it doesn't leave much room to step back.

Scorpio squares Aquarius, both fixed signs, and the friction makes something move. Water and air don't have a natural ease with each other, so feelings can arrive in a rush, or get held off for a long time and then arrive in a rush anyway. The Sun is in detriment in Aquarius, which is part of why warmth can feel like work for you. None of that means you feel less. It means you might need to find your own way into it, and that's fine.

In friendships, you might be surprised by how much you've missed someone. In the body, the card suggests going back to simple routines you had as a kid, early nights, a proper breakfast. At home you might find yourself playing music you haven't listened to since you were a teenager. With a sibling or cousin there might be a warm, unexpected exchange online. Write a letter to someone from your past, a real one, and post it.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed can make an Aquarius Moon step even further back from its feelings. You tell yourself you've moved on from your childhood, your family, your hometown, and in a way you have, though mostly you've boxed it up. The Sun in detriment here can make warmth feel like an effort, so you skip it and go straight to analysis. The square from Scorpio means the feeling doesn't go away.

It comes out sideways. You might get strangely upset at a film, or angry about a cause that has something to do with your own story. With family you might be friendly and distant at once. Pick one memory you usually tell as a funny story and tell it once as what it was.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising tends to come across as friendly but a little hard to pin down. Interesting, independent, slightly unusual. The Six of Cups adds a warmth people don't expect. You might seem like the kid from next door, someone people feel they can approach without an invitation. Aquarius rising usually wins people over with ideas, and with this card it's more likely to be kindness that does it.

The Sun is in detriment in Aquarius, so it has to work against the grain here, and with Aquarius rising that effort shows in your first impressions. Warmth might take you a moment. It comes out through odd, thoughtful gestures, remembering someone's favourite band, bringing them an article they'd like. Water and air are neutral elements, and here they've been introduced by something old, a shared memory, a name you both know. The square from Scorpio adds friction. Both signs are fixed and don't move easily, and you may feel a bit exposed being so openly sweet. People will like it, though.

In groups, you may be the one reconnecting old friends or organising the reunion. At work, a new colleague could turn out to share your hometown or your old school. With your style, you might go back to something you wore at sixteen, and it'll suit you. Tell someone you've just met about the neighbourhood you grew up in.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, this card can make Aquarius rising seem colder than you mean to be. You meet people with your detached, clever manner, and old friends seem like part of a life you've left. Or you're nostalgic in a way that feels ironic, retro clothes and old music worn as a pose, with no real feeling underneath. The Sun in detriment in your sign makes openness feel like effort, so you save it.

It turns up at reunions you skip, and in new places where you hold back until you're sure people are interesting enough. With colleagues, it can be keeping the conversation on ideas so nobody asks where you're from. Scorpio squares your rising sign, and sooner or later someone will push past it. Let them. When an old friend reaches out, answer within the day.

sun.upright:
Pisces and Scorpio are both water, four signs apart, and that trine gives the Six of Cups an easy way into a Pisces Sun. You already have a soft spot for the past, for old films, old friends, lost causes, and a way of remembering things as prettier than they were. I've met a lot of Pisces Suns who still have their school friendship bracelets. This card speaks your language.

The Sun doesn't have any dignity in Pisces, and it takes its colour from Jupiter (or Neptune, in modern charts), so it tends to shine through imagination and compassion. Water meeting water turns the volume up, which is lovely and also a lot. You might find old memories coming back with almost dreamlike detail, or feel drawn to people from your past you'd lost touch with. The risk is that it all gets a bit soft-focus, and a Pisces Sun can end up living in the memory for longer than is useful.

Creatively, this is a lovely card for you, art or music or writing that draws on childhood. With friends, someone gentle from the past may reappear. With money, watch for generosity that runs ahead of what you have, since the card is so openly giving. Make something, a drawing, a playlist, a short piece of writing, about one place you loved as a child.
sun.reversed:
Pisces Suns are good at escaping, and this card reversed turns the past into a place to escape to. The old days feel golden, the present feels hard, and you drift back to a time or a person that's gone. Water on water, with nothing to stop it, makes the drift easy. The Sun, coloured by Jupiter or Neptune here, makes the memory bigger and softer each time you visit it.

You'll see it in daydreams that take up hours and in re-reading old messages. It can come out with an ex, going back because of how it felt at the start. With money, it might be spending to recreate an old feeling. Ground yourself in one ordinary, present thing each day, a walk, a meal, a chore, done fully.

moon.upright:
Someone with the Moon in Pisces picks up on everyone's feelings and often can't tell which are theirs. For that Moon this is a warm bath of a card. Scorpio trines Pisces, water to water, and the feeling rises easily, kindness, nostalgia, old affection, a sense of being gently looked after. You might feel five years old again in the nicest possible way.

Because it's the same element, it's amplified, and for a Pisces Moon that means tenderness with very few edges. You might cry at an old song, or feel a sudden rush of love for someone you haven't seen since school. The Sun's warmth in this card comes through Jupiter's colouring in your sign (Neptune's, if you prefer the modern ruler), so it spreads and blurs. There's nothing wrong with that. Pisces Moons need soft places. Just check you're still eating properly and seeing people while you're in one.

In the body, sleep is where this shows up most, long dreams, the need for more of it. With family, a parent or grandparent might want to share old stories, and it's good to listen. In a relationship, you might long to be looked after the way you were as a small child. Spend an evening with old photos, and ring one person who's in them.
moon.reversed:
A Pisces Moon can be pulled under by this card reversed. Old feelings come back with no warning and no shape, and it's easy to spend days in a haze of memory, missing people, places, a version of your family that maybe never quite existed. Water on water means nothing slows it down. The Sun in your sign takes on Neptune's haze as well as Jupiter's size, which doesn't help.

It can come out in sleep, too much of it or dreams full of the past. It can come out as reaching for things that numb, too many late nights on the sofa with a screen. With family, it might be taking on everyone's old sadness as your own. Put some structure around the feeling, a set time to look through the old things and a set time to stop.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising gives a soft first impression anyway. Dreamy, kind, a bit hard to pin down. Add this card and you come across as someone with an old soul, the sort of person strangers feel they've met before. That's partly the trine. Scorpio and Pisces are both water and flow easily into each other, so the card sits comfortably on your surface.

The Sun is only visiting your sign and borrows its colour from Jupiter, or Neptune in modern charts, so its warmth comes through as kindness and openness. Water twice over makes it strong. You might find people telling you their stories within minutes of meeting you, or remembering you years later for a small kindness. Your instinct is to give, and it's a good instinct here. The only thing is that Pisces rising can give itself away to anyone who asks.

At work, you're likely to be the one who makes newcomers feel at home. In dating, someone could remind you of a childhood sweetheart. With friends, an old one might turn up at a new friend's party, and the two groups might get on. In your style, soft colours and something someone gave you will feel right. If someone new seems nervous, tell them about a time you felt the same.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising can drift with this card reversed, meeting people through a haze of nostalgia. You're wistful, a bit vague, half in some other time, and new people find you lovely and can't quite reach you. With water on water, there's nothing to give your first impression a firm edge. Scorpio's trine usually helps, and here it just makes it easier to slide back.

New jobs and new friendships are where you'll see it, since you're so busy being kind and agreeable that nobody knows what you want. Or you give too much too soon to someone who reminds you of the past. Before you say yes to anything new, take a day to think about whether you actually want it.

1.upright:
Something about how you carry yourself is going back to an earlier, less guarded setting. People might tell you that you look well, or that you seem more like your old self. The first house is your body, your face, the way you walk into things and how you begin, and with this card in it, what's live is a younger version of you. It isn't a sad thing. You're comfortable in yourself in a way you haven't been for a while.

The first house belongs naturally to Aries, and the Sun is exalted in Aries, so a Sun card is welcome here, honoured even. The trouble is the card's own sign. Scorpio sits a quincunx from Aries, five signs apart with nothing in common, and water meets fire in a house that likes to act fast. So you may feel pulled between wanting to start something new and wanting to feel your way back into something old. The first house is angular, a corner of the chart, so whatever you do about it will be seen.

In the body, this can be a return to an old sport, a haircut you had years ago, eating the way you did before life got busy. In how you start things, a way of working that came naturally to you at school might come back. People meeting you for the first time will find you warm. Pick up the physical activity you loved most as a kid and do it once a week for a while.
1.reversed:
The first house with this card reversed can show a self stuck in an old version of you. You dress the way you did ten years ago, walk into rooms with an attitude that fitted a younger person, and feel oddly out of step without knowing why. The quincunx between Scorpio and Aries makes it hard to adjust gracefully, and Mars, the natural ruler here, wants you moving while this card keeps turning you round.

It comes up in how you start things, relying on old habits, and in the body, pushing yourself the way you did at twenty-five. People who meet you might sense someone still living in an earlier chapter. Update one visible thing, clothes, glasses, the photo on your profile, so the outside matches who you are.

2.upright:
Money and what you're worth, in the plain sense of what's in the account and the less plain sense of what you think you deserve. That's the second house. Drawn here, this card usually points to money or support connected to the past, a family gift, an old debt repaid, something you'd forgotten you had. It can also be learning something about your worth from someone who knew you young.

The house belongs naturally to Taurus, which sits opposite Scorpio, so the card's sign is looking at this house from across the wheel. Taurus keeps, Scorpio shares and inherits, and the card pulls the two together. Water and earth get on well, which is good for slow, steady building. There's a tension too. Taking money from family can come with old strings attached, and you may feel the tug of them.

In practical terms, look at anything inherited, a bit of furniture, a savings account opened for you as a child, a skill passed down. With your self-worth, notice where you're still measuring yourself against what your parents earned. With a partner, it might be talking about the money habits you each grew up with. In spending, small generous gifts will feel better than big purchases. Sort out one family-related money matter you've been putting off.
2.reversed:
Nostalgia and money make an awkward pair, and in the second house this card reversed can mean spending to recreate a feeling. Buying the things you couldn't have as a child, holding onto an inheritance you can't bear to touch, or feeling that you'll never be as secure as you once were. The opposition from Scorpio means shared money and family ties are pulling on what's yours.

Bank statements tell the story, and so does the way you talk about money with family. It might be lending to a relative out of loyalty when you can't really afford it. It can also be undervaluing yourself because of a label someone gave you when you were young. Look at one regular expense and ask whether it's for the life you have or the one you had.

3.upright:
A brother or sister wants to talk about childhood, a neighbour turns out to know your family, or you catch yourself using a phrase your grandmother used. That's the Six of Cups in the third house, which covers siblings, everyday talk, short trips and learning. The past comes up in conversation, and mostly it's welcome.

The Moon has its joy here, which makes this a house for feeling and memory as well as talk, and that suits a card like this. The natural sign is Gemini, though, a quincunx from Scorpio, so there's a constant small adjustment between what you feel and how you say it. Water and air have to be introduced. You may find the words for something old come slowly, or come all at once in the car on the way somewhere.

With siblings, it's a good time for a proper chat, even about something you've never agreed on. In learning, you might return to something you studied as a kid. Short trips back to places you grew up could be worth more than they look. In texts and emails, a softer tone might creep in, and people will like it. Write or ring a sibling or cousin and start with a memory you share.
3.reversed:
Same old conversations, same old roles. In the third house, the card reversed can put you and a sibling straight back into the parts you played at ten, or have you retelling a story until it stops being true. The quincunx between the card's sign and Gemini makes it hard to find new words, so the old ones get used again and again. With the Moon rejoicing here, feelings sit close to the surface, which makes the old words sting more.

Family group chats and visits home are where it happens, and in a habit of learning only what you already know. It might be a neighbour or relative you stopped talking to over something small, years ago, and the silence has become a habit of its own. Next time the old argument starts, say something you've never said in it before.

4.upright:
Of all twelve houses, the fourth is probably where this card feels most at ease. It's home, roots, family, the private ground you stand on, and that's close to what the Six of Cups means anyway. The natural sign is Cancer, trine Scorpio, both water, so the card flows straight into this territory.

Water on water amplifies. The good side is a real sense of home, a family gathering that goes right, an old recipe coming out, a visit to where you grew up that leaves you steadier. The other side is that it can all be a bit much, grief for someone who used to be at the table, nostalgia for a house that's been sold. The Moon rules this house naturally, and the Sun in this card takes a quieter role than usual, lighting up memory. It's an angular house, so what happens at home tends to spill into everything else.

At home, you might want to put up old photos or bring out things from your childhood. With a parent, a conversation could bring you closer. In your own household, you might start a tradition from your family. Cook one dish from your family's history and share it with the people you live with, or whoever feels like home to you.
4.reversed:
The fourth house with this card reversed can be a home that's become a museum, or a family that only knows how to be together by going over the past.
