Water on water means the feelings pile up and nobody moves anything. The Moon, natural ruler of this house, keeps things, and here it keeps too much.

The house itself shows it, a room kept as someone left it, boxes you can't open. So do family roles, being treated as the youngest or the problem child long after it stopped being true. With a parent, it might mean going back to being who you were when you lived at home. Change one thing in your home that's been the same for years and see how it feels.

5.upright:
The Sun rules the fifth house, so a Sun card here is on home turf. This is play, creativity, romance, children, anything you do purely because you enjoy it, and this card shows children giving each other presents in a garden. It's one of the most natural houses for it. There's a joy here that feels a bit like being a kid again.

Venus has its joy in this house as well, so romance and pleasure do well. The friction is that Scorpio squares Leo, the house's natural sign, both fixed, and water and fire tend to fight. Leo wants to play out loud, and Scorpio wants depth and privacy. So your fun may come with more feeling attached than you're used to. A night out might turn into a long talk about the past, and a creative project might dig into something from your childhood you didn't plan to go near. It's still good, only deeper than you expected.

With children, your own or others', it's a lovely time to play the games you played. In romance, it can be a first love coming back or a date that feels like being a teenager. With a friend, it could be an afternoon of silliness neither of you expected. Creatively, go back to a medium you loved as a child, crayons, clay, a musical instrument, and make something with no purpose beyond enjoying it.
5.reversed:
Joy can get stuck in the past in the fifth house when this card is reversed. The fun you remember seems better than any you're having, or you're chasing a romance like one you had at seventeen. The square between Scorpio and Leo makes it hard to let go of how good it was, and with the Sun at home here, the pull is strong and so is the pride in it.

Romance is the usual place, going back to an ex, or comparing every date to someone from long ago. With children, it can be pushing them to love what you loved. Creatively, it can be redoing old work. Try something playful that you never did as a child, so there's no memory to measure it against.

6.upright:
The sixth house is the daily routine, the work you do day to day, and the body's upkeep, sleep, meals, the walk, the check-up you keep putting off. This card brings old habits back into the picture, the healthy ones especially. You might want to eat the way your family ate, or go back to a routine that kept you well when you were younger.

The house belongs naturally to Virgo, which sits sextile to Scorpio, and earth and water are friendly. So the card fits well here, as long as you take the opening. Mars has its joy in the sixth house, which means effort and hard work go well, and this is a gentle card that may soften the way you push yourself. There's some tension in that. You might be slower, kinder to yourself, and unsure whether that's allowed.

At work, a colleague from your past may help with something practical, or a newcomer may need you to show them how things are done. With your health, simple things work best, home-cooked meals, early nights, walking to places. Your desk or workspace might benefit from something that makes you smile, a photo, a mug someone gave you. Go back to one small daily habit you had as a child and keep it up.
6.reversed:
Comfort habits that have stopped working are the usual sign of this card reversed in the sixth house. The same takeaway, the same shows, the sofa after dinner, because it's what you've always done. Water and earth usually get on, and here the water has made the ground soft and slow. Mars rejoices in this house and wants some effort from you, and it isn't getting much.

At work, you might be doing things the way you were first taught, even when there's a better way. In the body, it might be tiredness from routines that soothe you without restoring anything, or old aches you've learnt to ignore because you've had them so long. Swap one comfort habit for something that actually leaves you feeling better afterwards.

7.upright:
Across the table in the seventh house sits the person you deal with one-to-one, a partner, a business partner, a close friend, even a rival. When this card lands here it often brings someone from the past, an ex, a childhood friend, a former colleague, or softens an existing relationship with memories of how you started. The house is angular, one of the corners of the chart, so these things tend to be visible.

The Sun is in fall in Libra, the seventh house's natural sign, so the card's way of shining doesn't come easily in this house. It has to find an indirect route. That usually means the warmth comes through small gestures between two people, the gift, the note, the favour. Scorpio is Libra's next-door neighbour, and the card's depth meets this house's fairness and charm. Air and water start as strangers here. You might want more closeness than the relationship is used to, and have to find a gentle way to ask for it.

With a partner, going back to where you met, or talking about what drew you to each other, can do a lot. In business, an old contact might become a partner again. With an ex, be careful and honest about what you're really missing. Tell your partner or closest friend one thing you loved about them when you first met.
7.reversed:
Holding a partner to how things were at the start is a common way this card shows up reversed in the seventh house. Or you're drawn back to an ex, or you keep choosing people who remind you of someone. With the Sun falling in Libra, the house's natural sign, your own needs go quiet in the relationship, and the past fills the gap. Water and air haven't been properly introduced, so feelings and words stay apart.

Comparisons give it away, the ex who did it better, the parent whose marriage you're copying without realising. In business, it can be sticking with a partnership out of loyalty. With friends, it might be one who still treats you as the person you were at school. Ask your partner what they need from you, and listen as if you'd just met.

8.upright:
This is the card's own territory. The eighth house belongs naturally to Scorpio, and this pip belongs to Scorpio, the Sun in the middle of that sign. The house covers the deep end of life, intimacy, sex, shared money, inheritances, grief, the things that end and what grows back after them. Nothing here is light, and the card doesn't try to make it light.

Water on water amplifies, and in this house that means a lot of feeling. What's live might be an inheritance, practical or emotional, from someone in the family. It might be grief for someone from your childhood that finally softens. In a relationship, it can be a new depth of trust, the kind that comes from knowing each other's history. The Sun in the card keeps it warm, though it's still deep water, and you may need more time alone than usual to take it in.

Shared money connected to family, a will, a joint account, a loan between relatives, is worth sorting out kindly. In intimacy it's tenderness and trust, closeness with someone who knows your past. With grief, it can be sorting through someone's things and finding something that makes you smile. Keep one object that belonged to someone you've lost somewhere you'll see it.
8.reversed:
The eighth house with this card reversed can hold onto old grief or old intimacy long after it's over. You might be keeping an ex's things, holding a family inheritance so tightly it causes a rift, or unable to let a relationship end properly. Scorpio is at home here, so the pull to keep hold is very strong. With water on water, nothing dries out, and old feelings stay as fresh as the day they started.

Wills and shared money are where it surfaces, and old family hurts come out with them. In intimacy, it can be carrying something from an old relationship into a new one. Let go of one thing you've kept only because you couldn't bear to lose it.

9.upright:
The Sun has its joy in the ninth house, the place it does its best work, which gives this Sun card more strength here than you might expect. The ninth is belief, study, long trips and the big ideas you live by. What's live is meaning drawn from the past, the values you were raised with, the teacher who changed how you saw things, somewhere overseas you went when you were young.

The natural sign is Sagittarius, the sign right after Scorpio, and neighbours like that have little in common. Fire and water don't mix easily either. Sagittarius wants to go further, and Scorpio wants to go deeper. So there's a pull between looking ahead and looking back. You might find a belief from childhood looks different now, kinder or less certain, or that you want to go back to a place you travelled to years ago and see it with older eyes.

In study, you might return to a subject you gave up. In travel, a trip back somewhere familiar can teach you more than a new one. With faith or philosophy, it's worth revisiting what your family believed and deciding what you keep. With someone from another country, a shared memory of home could start a real friendship. Look up an old teacher or mentor and tell them what stuck.
9.reversed:
Beliefs you grew up with can get clung to in the ninth house when this card is reversed, because they're familiar, even if they no longer fit. Or it's the opposite, rejecting everything you were taught without looking at what was good in it. Fire and water are opposed, so the feeling and the belief don't meet. The Sun has its joy here and wants to shine through understanding, and it can't while the view is fixed on the past.

Arguments about politics or faith with family are one sign, and travel is another, always going back to the same place. In study, it might be sticking to what you already know. Write down one belief you inherited and, honestly, whether you'd choose it again.

10.upright:
Career, reputation, your public role, what you're known for. The tenth house is the top of the chart. Drawn into the tenth, the card usually means the past helping your work, an old contact, a former boss, a skill from years back, or work that connects to childhood, teaching, care, anything with young people.

The house belongs naturally to Capricorn, which is sextile Scorpio, and water and earth work well together. So this is a cooperative placement, as long as you use it. Saturn, the natural ruler, likes things earned, and it can feel strange to get help just because someone remembers you. It's still earned, in a way. You did something good years ago, and people haven't forgotten. The tenth is an angular house, so what happens here is visible, and the kindness in this card gets seen as well. Some people find that awkward at work. It usually helps.

Practically, this favours getting back in touch with people you've worked with, updating an old reference, or going back to a field you left. Your reputation might benefit from a story about where you started. With a parent, especially one who shaped your ambitions, a conversation about your work could be warm. Send a thank-you to the person who gave you your first real chance.
10.reversed:
Resting on old success is the risk in the tenth house with this card upside down. The award, the big project, the job you had when you were at your best. You keep leaning on it, or you're measuring every new role against that one. Saturn, which rules this house naturally, doesn't reward coasting, and the sextile between the card's sign and Capricorn needs something new from you to work with.

Job interviews full of old stories are one sign. Staying somewhere out of loyalty when the work isn't growing you is another. With colleagues, you could end up repeating how things used to be done. Or it's the career a parent wanted for you, followed out of duty. Update your CV so the most recent thing you're proud of is at the top.

11.upright:
Old friends coming back into view is the most common way this card shows up in the eleventh house. A school friend on social media, a reunion, a group you belonged to years ago that gets back together. The eleventh is friends, networks and the hopes you have for the future, your people outside the family.

Jupiter has its joy in the eleventh house, so friendship tends to be generous here. The awkward part is that Aquarius, this house's natural sign, is where the Sun sits in detriment, so the card's warmth has to work against the grain. Scorpio squares Aquarius as well, both fixed. So you might love seeing old friends and still feel a little out of place, as if you've changed and they haven't, or the other way round. That's normal. It takes a few meetings to find the new version of an old friendship.

With friends, it's a good time to reconnect with someone you drifted from. In groups, you might go back to a club, team or community you used to be part of. With your hopes, look at a dream you had when you were younger and see if some of it is still worth chasing. Organise a small get-together with old friends, even if only two people come.
11.reversed:
Old friendships that have stopped growing are what this card reversed tends to show in the eleventh house. You meet the same people, tell the same stories, and feel a bit hollow afterwards. Or you're avoiding new friends because nobody can match the ones from school. The square from Scorpio makes it hard to move on, though Jupiter, which rejoices here, wants the circle to widen.

Group chats and reunions show it, and so do hopes you haven't updated since your twenties. It can also be staying in a group out of loyalty when you've quietly outgrown it. With the Sun in detriment in Aquarius, warmth in groups can feel like hard work. Say yes to one invitation from someone you don't know well yet.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the hidden part of the chart. Sleep, dreams, solitude, what you keep to yourself, and what you're not aware of yet. What this card brings to it is private memory. Old feelings come up in dreams or quiet moments, and you might find yourself thinking about people and places you haven't thought of in years.

The natural sign is Pisces, trine Scorpio, both water, so the card flows easily into this house. Same element, so it's amplified, which here means a lot going on beneath the surface. Saturn has its joy in the twelfth, and it gives this house some structure, a need for time alone that's actually good for you. You might want to withdraw a bit and sort through the past on your own. That's healthy, as long as you come back. The Sun in this card keeps the hidden things warm, so what comes up is more likely to comfort you than frighten you.

In sleep, you might dream of childhood homes or old friends. On your own, going through old boxes or photos can do you good. A family secret might come to light, gently. If you help others quietly, volunteering or caring for someone, it'll feel meaningful. Spend an afternoon on your own with something from your past, and write down what comes up.
12.reversed:
In the twelfth house, this card reversed can mean hiding in the past. Daydreams, old photos, old songs, hours spent in memory because it's easier than being in the present. Water on water means it's easy to drift a long way without noticing, and the trine from Scorpio usually makes this house a comfort, which is exactly why it's easy to stay too long.

It shows in sleep, too much or too little, and in avoiding people. It can also be a private grief you haven't told anyone about. Saturn rejoices here and would like some shape to your time alone. Without it, retreat turns into hiding. Set a limit on how long you spend in old things, and when the time's up, go and do something with someone.
